To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a blockchain-based consensus protocol with “common prefix” property can tolerate adversarial hashing power up to 1/2; 2) “chain quality” can be used to achieve fast and robust PKI setup; and 3) a blockchain-based transaction ledger can be constructed with a single “genesis” block and no pre-computation, while still being robust against adversarial hashing power 1/2.
the blockchain data structure is sufficient for consensus and that a robust public ledger is possible without any trusted party.
(a) the blockchain data structure is a useful abstraction, and (b) the blockchain can be bootstrapped in a decentralized fashion, without the need of an external trusted setup.

the following question: what are the fundamental properties of the Bitcoin blockchain and how can they be used to build robust protocols on top of them?

“bootstrapping” the Bitcoin blockchain.

Bitcoin is secure, but not provable so.

the Bitcoin backbone protocol is a secure, practical and scalable solution to the consensus and public transaction ledger problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is the first work that gives provable security for Bitcoin-like protocols.
it provides a rigorous and general framework to analyze the security of Bitcoin-like protocols.
